walkthroughs.body_html:
Algorithms — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Algorithms brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Algorithms.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Dijkstra's algorithm fails when edges have...
options: Equal weights
Negative weights
Integer weights
Real weights

mcqs.q: What does the 'h' in A*'s f(n) = g(n) + h(n) represent?
options: History cost
Heuristic estimate to goal
Hash value
Heap depth

mcqs.q: What is the worst-case complexity of bubble sort?
options: O(n) because it just passes through the list.
It is impossible to break.
O(n squared).
O(log n).

mcqs.q: What is the denary value of binary 10110?
options: It is impossible to break.
10110 (treating it as a denary number).
11 (counting the 1s).

mcqs.q: What is the main advantage of asymmetric encryption?
options: 11 (counting the 1s).
It is faster than symmetric encryption.
It is impossible to break.
Secure key exchange without sharing a secret in advance.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “A* search”?
options: A finite, deterministic, unambiguous sequence of steps that solves a problem in finite time.
Best-first graph search using f(n) = g(n) + h(n); guaranteed optimal with an admissible heuristic.
Finds shortest paths from a source node in a graph with non-negative edge weights.
Makes the locally optimal choice at each step (e.g., Dijkstra), hoping for a global optimum.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Greedy algorithm”?
options: Tries candidate solutions and abandons (backtracks) any that cannot be completed - used in N-queens, sudoku.
A finite, deterministic, unambiguous sequence of steps that solves a problem in finite time.
Finds shortest paths from a source node in a graph with non-negative edge weights.
Makes the locally optimal choice at each step (e.g., Dijkstra), hoping for a global optimum.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Algorithm”?
options: Best-first graph search using f(n) = g(n) + h(n); guaranteed optimal with an admissible heuristic.
Tries candidate solutions and abandons (backtracks) any that cannot be completed - used in N-queens, sudoku.
Makes the locally optimal choice at each step (e.g., Dijkstra), hoping for a global optimum.
A finite, deterministic, unambiguous sequence of steps that solves a problem in finite time.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Divide and conquer”?
options: A finite, deterministic, unambiguous sequence of steps that solves a problem in finite time.
Tries candidate solutions and abandons (backtracks) any that cannot be completed - used in N-queens, sudoku.
Algorithmic strategy splitting a problem into independent subproblems, solving recursively then combining.
Makes the locally optimal choice at each step (e.g., Dijkstra), hoping for a global optimum.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Backtracking”?
options: Makes the locally optimal choice at each step (e.g., Dijkstra), hoping for a global optimum.
A finite, deterministic, unambiguous sequence of steps that solves a problem in finite time.
Tries candidate solutions and abandons (backtracks) any that cannot be completed - used in N-queens, sudoku.
Best-first graph search using f(n) = g(n) + h(n); guaranteed optimal with an admissible heuristic.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Dijkstra's algorithm”?
options: Algorithmic strategy splitting a problem into independent subproblems, solving recursively then combining.

A finite, deterministic, unambiguous sequence of steps that solves a problem in finite time.
